script: My brother deleted my save file the night before I was going to finish the game. Two hundred and eleven hours. He did not do it out of spite, which honestly would have been easier. He was twelve, he wanted one save slot for himself, and the console said the drive was full. I found out at six in the morning. The slot just said empty. I did not yell at him. I did not talk to him for nine days, which was worse, and we both knew it. He left a note under my door on the fourth day that just said sorry, in pencil. I kept it. I never told him that. What I did not know was what he did with those nine days. He took the bus to the game store and asked what a used copy cost. He did not have the money. So he asked if there was any other way, and the guy behind the counter told him some people just replay it. That was the whole answer. So my brother started the game from zero on his own account, and he played it every day after school while I was at practice, and he did not tell me. He was not trying to beat it. He was trying to get my save back to where it was. He reached hour forty before he understood he could not give me his progress. That is not how the console works. Two accounts, two files, no transfer. He found that out on a forum and he cried in the bathroom so I would not hear it. My mother told me that part years later. On the ninth day he knocked and asked if I wanted to see something. He had his account loaded, and he had built the exact starting camp I had built, in the same order, from memory, because he had watched me do it for two hundred hours from the floor of my room. He said he could not give it back. He could only show me he had been paying attention the whole time. I sat down on the floor next to him. We started over on my account together that night. He is twenty three now. He still has the note I kept.
